findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers
findings.body: Fallback loading is triggered solely by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because the translate accelerator lazy-loads only `config.locale` (see `translate` in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), any translation performed outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, user notification emails, scheduled tasks — will have the current locale's file loaded but never the fallback chain (site default locale and :en). In those contexts a key missing from the user's locale will render as 'translation missing' instead of falling back to the default/English string, so the feature only works for HTTP requests and silently no-ops elsewhere. The fallback loading should happen inside the translation path (e.g., in `load_locale`/`translate` or `I18n.with_locale`) rather than in a controller before_filter.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain, so cached results go stale when default_locale changes or differs per site
findings.body: The accelerator caches no-argument translations under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Before this change, the translation for a given key+locale depended only on that locale's file; now it also depends on the fallback chain, which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale` (see `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in config/initializers/i18n.rb). The cache is only cleared by `I18n.reload!`, which a site-setting change does not trigger. Consequences: (1) after an admin changes the site default locale, keys missing in a user's locale keep serving strings from the old default locale until the process restarts; (2) on multisite installs where different sites share the process and backend but have different `default_locale` values, a fallback result cached for one site is served to another site with a different default locale, producing wrong-language output. The cache key needs to incorporate the effective fallback list (or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes).

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the chain on every translation lookup
findings.body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation that reaches the backend (which is all translations with interpolation arguments, since the LRU cache only covers the no-args path). The overridden `[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` lookup, allocates a symbol via `to_sym`, allocates and `uniq`s an array on every call, even though the result only changes when `default_locale` changes. On translation-heavy pages this is pure per-call overhead. Consider memoizing the computed list and invalidating it when the default_locale setting changes.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback ordering and loading behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), replaces the global `I18n.fallbacks` object with a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, moves pluralization setup between initializers, and adds `ensure_loaded!` to the translation accelerator, but changes no spec files (the PR description is also just the placeholder 'Test 9'). There is no coverage verifying that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the default locale and then to English, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` behaves correctly when the user locale equals the default locale, or that fallback locale files actually get loaded. A regression here would surface as untranslated UI strings and would be easy to miss without tests.
